title: Credit Already Issued on a Northbeam Renew Trade-In Agreement, Taken Off at Close-Out
content:
The credit already issued on the agreement is read from the trade-in history and taken off, so that a batch is never paid for twice. Two figures are read from the Northbeam Renew Trade-In agreement's own trade-in history: the trade-in credit issued on it, and the credit written off where unspent credit has expired on it.

1. Where credit has been issued on the agreement and no expiry of unspent credit stands on it, the credit already issued on the agreement is taken off in full.
2. Where credit has been issued on the agreement and an expiry of unspent credit stands on it, the credit already issued less the credit written off at that expiry is taken off, the difference being rounded to the cent.
3. Where no credit has been issued on the agreement, nothing is taken off on that account.

**Points of judgement.**

- Credit has been issued on the agreement where the trade-in history carries credit above nothing; where it carries none, the third branch governs whatever else stands on the history.
- An expiry of unspent credit stands on the agreement where the history carries credit written off above nothing.
- The write-off reduces what is taken off, because that much of the earlier credit is no longer in the customer's hands.

**Hypothetical illustrations.** An agreement carrying 1475.00 USD of credit issued and no expiry has 1475.00 USD taken off. The same agreement with 312.50 USD written off at an expiry has 1162.50 USD taken off. An agreement carrying no credit issued has nothing taken off, whether or not any write-off stands on it.
